Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] – references underwriting activity 2016–2019, UNESCO 2016 report, November mercury/arsenic study
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] – ORBC complaint assessment pending
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] – climate impact, sea level rise, environmental degradation, banking policy shifts on fossil fuel financing

Synopsis:
    Three complainants from the Sundarbans region have filed a formal complaint with the UK's Office for Responsible Business Conduct against Barclays Bank, alleging it breached international guidelines by underwriting NTPC Ltd and Export-Import Bank of India bonds linked to the Rampal coal-fired power plant. The plant sits adjacent to the Sundarbans UNESCO World Heritage Site, where recent studies show elevated heavy-metal contamination in waterways. Complainants argue Barclays failed adequate due diligence on environmental and human rights risks, and that the plant's emissions exacerbate climate vulnerability in an already at-risk region. The case highlights growing pressure on European banks to exit fossil fuel financing, particularly coal, and redirect capital toward renewables.
